name: Chin Tuck
steps: Sit or stand tall and look straight ahead.
Glide your chin straight back, as if making a gentle double chin.
Hold for three seconds, then relax and repeat.
caution: Keep the movement small and pain-free — glide back, never force the head down.

name: Neck Side Stretch
steps: Sit tall and let your right ear drop toward your right shoulder.
For a little more stretch, rest your right hand lightly on your head.
Hold, return slowly to centre, then change sides.
caution: A gentle pull is enough. Never yank the head, and back off if you feel tingling.

name: Wall Slide
steps: Stand with your back against a wall, arms in a goalpost position.
Slide your arms slowly up the wall as far as they go without pinching.
Lower back to the goalpost with the same control.
caution: Keep your ribs down and lower back relaxed — shrink the range if the shoulder pinches.

name: Doorway Chest Stretch
steps: Stand in a doorway with your forearms on the frame, elbows at shoulder height.
Step one foot through until you feel a stretch across the chest.
Breathe slowly and hold, then step back to release.
caution: Ease off if you feel pins and needles in the hands — that is a nerve, not a muscle.

name: Cat–Camel
steps: Start on hands and knees, hands under shoulders, knees under hips.
Round your back up toward the ceiling and let your head drop.
Then let your belly sink and lift your chest, flowing slowly between the two.
caution: Stay in a comfortable range — this should feel like oiling the spine, not stretching hard.

name: Bird Dog
steps: From hands and knees, reach one arm forward and the opposite leg back.
Keep your hips level and hold for one slow breath.
Return with control and swap sides.
caution: Keep the lower back flat like a table — reach less far if it starts to arch or twist.

name: Glute Bridge
steps: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet hip-width apart.
Press through your heels and lift your hips into one straight line from shoulders to knees.
Hold for two seconds, then lower slowly.
caution: Lift only as high as the hips go without arching the lower back.

name: Half-Kneel Hip Flexor Stretch
steps: Kneel on one knee with the other foot flat in front — pad the knee with a cushion.
Tuck your tailbone slightly and shift your weight gently forward.
Feel the stretch across the front of the kneeling hip and hold.
caution: The stretch belongs at the front of the hip — if the lower back pinches, tuck and shorten.

name: Sit to Stand
steps: Sit toward the front of a firm chair with your feet under your knees.
Lean forward and push through the whole foot to stand tall.
Lower back down slowly, tapping the seat before you rise again.
caution: Keep the knees tracking over the toes, and use the armrests only if you truly need them.

name: Heel Raise
steps: Stand tall with your fingertips on a wall or counter for balance.
Rise up onto the balls of your feet as high as comfortable.
Lower back down slowly over three seconds.
caution: If both legs feel easy, ask us before progressing to the single-leg version.
